trials.label: changes_requested
trials.detail: Both endpoints are implemented, registered in http.Register and covered by handler tests: owner-only create, a 201 response with an opaque crypto/rand hex token, and 404 for unknown or expired tokens. ShareButton copies `/share/<token>` and shows an error when copying fails, with tests for both. The JSON fields match packages/contract ShareLink. I found only minor gaps: some error branches have no tests, and every store error from schedule lookup is reported as 404.

trials.label: changes_requested
trials.detail: Routes are wired and tokens are opaque random hex, but POST /schedules/:id/share never checks ownership, so any caller can create a share link for any schedule. That is a security hole and fails the 'only the owner' criterion. The tests can't be trusted either: `make test` is `true`, so no Go or web test actually ran. The Go test file uses helpers that are never defined (assertStatus, post, get, owner, tok), and so does the web test (render, click, screen, clipboard mock). Errors from rand.Read, Links().Save and the clipboard write are dropped without handling, and the clipboard-failure path required by the web task is missing.

trials.label: changes_requested
trials.detail: Routes are wired, but the work doesn't integrate. The web ShareButton reads `link.expires_at`, while the shared contract (and the button's own test) uses `expiresAt`, so the button always shows "valid until undefined". The API also returns only `{token}`, not the ShareLink shape the web consumes. The passing verify proves nothing: `make test` is `true`, the Go tests rely on helpers that exist nowhere in the repo, and several required tests are missing (unknown schedule 404, expired token 404, copy failure).
